paper.title_en: Early Near-Infrared Excess and Rapid Disk-Corona Evolution in the Tidal Disruption Event 2024aepd
paper.abstract_en: We present multi-wavelength observations of the tidal disruption event (TDE) 2024aepd, spanning primarily the first $\sim$300 days after discovery. A prominent near-infrared (NIR) excess is detected as early as $\sim$40 days. Its nearly flat power-law spectrum strongly deviates from the Rayleigh-Jeans tail of the UV-optical blackbody. Although a conventional dust-echo origin cannot be completely ruled out, free-free emission from a reprocessing photospheric envelope provides a more plausible explanation. The spectral break between the UV-optical and NIR components shifts to higher frequencies, while the inferred density-profile index remains nearly constant, suggesting evolving reprocessing conditions within a broadly unchanged density structure. In addition, the X-ray spectrum is initially dominated by a thermal disk component accompanied by a hard excess. From $\sim$178 days onward, the spectrum becomes power-law dominated and subsequently hardens, indicating the rapid emergence and strengthening of a hot corona. These results provide evidence for frequency-dependent reprocessing at early times and for the rapid development of a disk-corona system, placing new constraints on the structure and evolution of the reprocessing layer around supermassive black holes.
